I remember we had an average of one or two fat kids in my elementary classes, They were also the dumb kids. I don't know if that's related, but it's the truth. For the rest of us fat was not an option. Starting at the age of eight I walked or rode my bike two miles to school. Then after school we went and shot hoops and hung out at the boys and girls club, or in later years skateboarded around town. Our parents did not approve of kids being indoors for any length of time, TV sucked, the internet didn't exist, and since we didn't have anything else to do we would ride around to each others houses till we had enough kids to play smear the queer, race the train, or mailbox baseball. Once a week we just ran around the damn soccer field til we hit a mile, then we could do whatever else we wanted, We had a game, whenever we passed one of the kids walking instead of running we would shout "LAAAAAAAP" so that everyone knew that we had just passed the poor kid again. "LAAAAP" "LAAAAAAP" "LAAAAAAAAAAAP" By the end of PE all the normal kids would be playing soccer or basketball while the unfit trudged their lonely circuit of shame. My god we were such assholes, but the truth is if you wanted a social life it was keep up or drop out.

Of course exercise alone will not help you if you eat like a marmot, so I think back to my diet. We ate actual meals, we didn't have a microwave in the house till I was about 14 years old. I had to cook my damn meals, that took planning, preparation and teamwork. At some time in the 90's fat free food became a huge fad that never faded, suddenly recipes are calling for less fat and much more sugar. Go look at an old copy of "The joy of Cooking" from the 1960's and compare it to today's instant meals. Sugar is a insidious thing; If I eat a massive cheeseburger for lunch my body knows it's good on calories for a while and says, "Salad for dinner tonight folks" But, I can't fill up on sweet shit. Simple carbohydrates don't seem to register on my bodies fuel gauge and that is a huge part of the modern diet. Take a look at the carb content of energy drinks or frozen dinners and just picture in your mind preparing this for your family by measuring out tablespoons of sugar and starch; you wouldn't do it, but the frozen foods are calorie trojan horses and that is what people are eating now. Since I'm an adult I know to watch out for this, but when I was 10 I was a lazy unmotivated and did not give a damn, I could easily have slipped into the trap of eating out of boredom, or endless snacking in front of the screen.

But, I had parents. My parents loved me very much, but they did not really love being parents. There was a natural order of needs in the house. Grown up problems were taken seriously, kid problems were not. Cause problems for the adults, and they will give you real problems to deal with. I was not a special snowflake, I was a "joyful burden" as a minister once put it. There was a strong sense in our protestant community that too much love and care could be as crippling to a young boy as too little. As a young member of our church I did not have full responsibilities, but I knew that my actions would reflect on my parents, and the church minded each others business. If little Johnny was making a pig of himself at the church hospitality after the service; the church ladies would make comments to that effect and hell has no fury like a mother embarrassed in front of her peers.

My family was very loving, but they never expressed it in a material way. We spent time together, read books together, listened to the radio and hunted mammoths as a family. Looking at the younger members of my family right now, The kids are getting fat because the adults are getting fat. Everyone is making independant meal choices. It's so easy and so cheap to just grab something out of the freezer or cupboard that nobody is eating the same meal at mealtime, I also notice that disorganised eating is very common, one meal a day might be a sit down affair while the rest of the day is spent grazing. Everyone is too busy to really cook and food is just a button push away, so meals are as easy as entertainment at this point.When I was a boy, you did not eat unless it was mealtime or you would 'spoil your appetite'. I ate what everyone else ate, I didn't have food that I liked purchased for me, special meals were for birthdays.

I think some of us just self regulate well and some people don't. There was a time in 1820's America when the per capita hard liquor consumption was ~4 gallons per person per year. This was the birth of cheap booze and like the birth of cheap food today it caused a huge health crisis. Over time society has adjusted and our perceptions of drunkenness have evolved. I predict our perceptions of food will also evolve. In time the town fat person may be viewed with as much pity and disgust as the town drunk is today. Until then get the fuck off my lawn.

Born in 1979. In elementary school, nobody was fat. I blanked out most of junior high. In high school, my class had The Fat Kid. He really was, too. Our desks were all one piece that you sort of slid into, and he needed a special one. I don't know what to blame for the epidemic, but it really is a recent thing.

There were several factors:

1) We were fucking ACTIVE. We had way more recess, way more lunch, and Phys. Ed. was fucking Phys. Ed. We were expected to run, do all manner of shit during those classes.

When we got home and during the summer, we ran and biked everywhere. At or around dawn or early in the day we'd take off and hare around doing shit, and the rule was be back on the doorstep at or before the streetlights came on. We didn't park ourselves in front of an Xbox. I conservatively estimate I'd bicycle at least 10-15 miles a day in the summer simply going back and forth to and from friends' houses.

2) If you slept over at a friend's house, you ate dinner before you went there, or if you were invited to dinner as part of it, it was an actual dinner. It was very, very, very rarely "here's $20, go buy tons of Domino's."

3) We kids had a lot less money back then. I remember MAYBE US having 20, 25 cents after spending much of an afternoon finding discarded Coke bottles some teenagers were too lazy to take back for the deposit. That bought maybe five Twizzlers, and the sugar off that was burned real quick as we would then bicycle 2 miles off to a friend's house to swim for several hours in a pool. I see kids walking around with a LOT more money now.

4) Shit was made with sugar, not HFCS, and a lot less sweeter. Fewer snack foods. Keep in mind that snacks weren't as readily available. You can throw a pizza pocket into a microwave, but back in the day you had to turn on an oven, keep the oven on while it heated up, then stick the frozen pizza into the oven.
